clusters.name: Buying a franchise (generic)
clusters.description: An aspiring owner buys into an established franchise system for its brand, playbook and support, paying an upfront fee plus ongoing royalties and keeping the operating profit.

clusters.name: Single-unit restaurant/food franchise
clusters.description: An owner operates one location of a known food brand (Subway, McDonald's, Crumbl, etc.) selling to walk-in consumers, earning store profit after franchise fees and royalties.

clusters.name: Multi-unit / multi-brand franchise development
clusters.description: A portfolio operator builds many franchise locations across one or more brands using operating partners and outside capital, earning returns from unit operations.

clusters.name: Fitness club/studio franchise
clusters.description: An owner operates a fitness franchise such as Planet Fitness or Orangetheory, earning recurring membership revenue under the franchisor's brand.

clusters.name: Residential cleaning franchise
clusters.description: An owner runs a home-cleaning business under a brand such as Molly Maid or Two Maids for homeowners, earning service revenue minus royalties.

clusters.name: Estate sale franchise
clusters.description: An owner pays $50-75k to join an estate sale franchise for leads, training and brand, earning commission on estate sales minus royalties.

clusters.name: Lawn care / grounds maintenance franchise
clusters.description: An owner runs a Grounds Guys-style mowing and grounds franchise for residential and commercial properties, earning recurring service fees.

clusters.name: Tutoring learning-centre franchise
clusters.description: An owner operates a Mathnasium centre for students and families, earning tuition fees using the franchisor's curriculum and brand.

clusters.name: Waxing/beauty service franchise
clusters.description: An owner operates a European Wax Center location for beauty-service customers, earning service and membership revenue.

clusters.name: Franchising your own business concept
clusters.description: An owner of a proven local business (laundromat, party rental, power washing, restaurant, golf simulator, cake campaigns) sells franchises or territories to other operators and earns franchise fees, royalties or a revenue split.

clusters.name: Business-in-a-box coffee carts on revenue share
clusters.description: You supply the coffee cart, stock and location to side-gig operators and take about 30% of revenue through your own payment account.
